text: The City seeks implementation and integration of Oracle ERP and Utility Billing solutions

citations.text: The purpose of this request for proposal (RFP) is to invite qualified implementation partners to submit a proposal for the deployment and integration of Oracle's Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Utility Billing solutions for the City of Durham in North Carolina (the City).
This RFP outlines the City’s specific requirements regarding the implementation, customization, and operational integration of the Oracle solution.

text: The project includes Oracle ERP, HCM, and Utility Billing implementation

citations.text: The City has gone through extensive due diligence to select Oracle ERP as the chosen Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Human Capital Management (HCM) and Utility Billing solution.

The first part of this engagement with Info-Tech was focused on building a clear vision and strategy for ERP, HCM and Utility Billing System; and the second part was to evaluate and select the ERP, HCM and Utility Billing solution, and subsequently a competent implementation partner.

text: The City wants local-government Oracle expertise, especially utility billing, customer accounts, meter reading, and billing processes

citations.text: The City requires a partner with proven expertise in effectively implementing Oracle's solutions, particularly in areas critical to local government operations such as utility billing (including customer accounts management, meter reading, and customer billing processes).

text: The City wants a partner to turn defined future business processes and IT requirements into a working Oracle environment

citations.text: The project continues to be strategically aligned with the City's business vision and goals, ensuring that the implementation phase is driven by the business requirements previously established.

The focus is now on partnering with a capable and experienced Oracle implementation partner, who will be instrumental in transforming the defined future business processes and IT requirements into a fully functional Oracle environment.

text: The City wants efficient timely reporting, integrated processes, and consistent corporate data across Finance, Budget and Management Services, Customer Billing Services, and Human Resources

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: To support the City’s strategic direction, a solution must have the ability to produce efficient and timely reports to internal and external stakeholders, to integrate business processes, and to provide consistent corporate data across various users in multiple departments including the Finance Department, Budget & Management Services Department, The Customer Billing Services Division within the Department of Water Management, and Human Resources.

text: The City has unintegrated systems, unsupported applications, manual processes, and limited reporting capabilities

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: The City operates in an environment of largely unintegrated disparate systems, some of which are unsupported and lack reporting capabilities.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: The City operates through a significant amount of manual interaction from users across the entire organization.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: In addition, some strategic processes are poorly supported by the existing technologies.

text: The City reports multiple systems of record, duplicated data, reconciliation work, inconsistent information, and limited data-driven decisions

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Multiple systems of record resulting in the duplication of data, complicating data availability, cross checking, and reporting.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Manual processes and lack of visibility into disparate systems creating inconsistent information.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Time-consuming data reconciliation processes and lack of visibility into disparate systems, creating inconsistent answers to the same questions.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • The inability to make data-driven business decisions due to the absence of aggregate data from a single integrated, reliable set of information.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Increased resource effort spent on non-value-added functions (e.g., re-keying, data validation, tracing transactions).
